newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: FRENCH COMPANY SEEKS PERMISSION FOR URANIUM MINE
Negotiations have re-opened to try to win approval for a Northern Territory uranium deposit to be mined, 15 years after the mine was first given the go-ahead.
A lease was granted for the Koongarra deposit, west of the proposed Jabiluka mine, 10 years before Kakadu National Park was declared.
Former leaseholders, Dennison, received environmental approvals and Aboriginal consent for the mine 15 years ago, but it was not up-and-running before Labor's victory in the 1983 election.

French company, Cogema, which has acquired the lease, has confirmed it is holding talks with the Northern Land Council, which represents Koongarra's traditional owners, with the aim of approving the mine.
MOMENTUM BUILDS FOR HMAS SYDNEY SELECT COMMITTEE
Actor Jack Thompson has joined the call for the House of Representatives to establish a Select Committee inquiry into the sinking of H-M-A-S Sydney.
A similar motion was tabled in Parliament by West Australian MPs, Stephen Smith and Paul Filing, about three months ago, and will be debated in the House today.
More than 600 crew on the Sydney died when the vessel was attacked by the German raider, Kormoran, off the coast of Geraldton in November 1941.
H-M-A-S Sydney Foundation Trust Chairman, Ed Punchard, says the call for the committee is just part of a move to ensure that the sailors on the Sydney are properly remembered.
Mr Punchard says there is renewed hope a select committee will be formed.
JABILUKA MINE ROW COMING TO A HEAD

The environmental impact statement for the Jabiluka uranium mine, proposed for the Northern Territory, is to be handed to the Federal Government tomorrow, amid attempts to stop the mine from going ahead.
Traditional owners of the proposed mine site last week lodged a case with the Federal Court, which argues the mining lease is invalid.
In line with this, they have asked the Jabiluka developer, Energy Resources of Australia, to stop paying royalties for the lease.
Environmental groups also oppose the mine's development, saying it will compromise the World Heritage values of the neighbouring Kakadu National Park.
However, the construction union is supporting the mine, because of the jobs it will create.
PM'S NATIVE TITLE PLAN "ALL WRONG"
The Northern Land Council is today expected to urge industry representatives to use their power to convince the Federal Government to rethink its native title plans.
In a paper to be presented to a conference in Brisbane, Galarrwuy Yunupingu says a sector of the pastoral industry has hijacked the native title debate.
In the paper, Mr Yunupingu says the Prime Minister's 10 point plan is all wrong, and says John Howard should start again.
He says Aboriginal people will not allow their native title rights to be taken away, and Mr Howard's plan will lead to lengthy legal and constitutional challenges if it is enacted.
Mr Yunupingu says the National Indigenous Working Group has developed a workable response to the High Court's Wik decision, which found native title existed on pastoral leases.
He says indigenous people are not powerless - they hold the key to native title resolution, whether via negotiated outcomes or via the courts.
CHAMBER OF COMMERCE SAYS INTEREST RATES WILL STAY LOW
The Chamber of Commerce and Industry says while official interest rates may fall again very soon, they are not expected to increase for some time.
The chamber says in a flat economy, there cannot be any real justification for raising rates and slowing economic activity.
It says rates rises stopped the economy at the start of the decade, and a second round in 1994 is the reason the economy remains flat and unemployment high.
The chamber says it will be some time before unemployment falls below eight per cent.
COALITION MPS TO DISCUSS TAX REFORM
National and Liberal party MPs will meet with the Prime Minister tonight on tax reform.
The forum will discuss how far tax reform should go, whether it should include a GST, social welfare concerns and political tactics to maximise popular acceptance of change.

The Prime Minister and Treasurer have raised the option of a Goods and Services Tax, and National Party leader, Tim Fischer, says he wants an end to fuel taxes and sales tax on all exports, replaced by a rebateable form of GST.
West Australian Premier, Richard Court, says tax reform must address state taxes and wants an end to payroll tax to tackle unemployment.
WA INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS LAWS "BREACH CONVENTIONS"
The International Labour Organisation has found Western Australia's labour relations laws breach three international conventions signed by Australia.
The Trades and Labour Council asked the I-L-O to comment on the laws before they were passed through the West Australian Parliament last month.
The ILO says the new laws will prevent workers from expressing, promoting and defending their economic and social interests.
TLC Secretary, Tony Cooke, says while the comments are informal at this stage, they are critical of all aspects of the laws.
BOATPEOPLE LIKELY TO HAVE BEEN HEADING TO SYDNEY
A Torres Strait resident who gave food to one of the illegal immigrants who landed in the Strait last week says the man indicated to her he was from China and heading to Sydney.
136 other boatpeople have been flown to the Port Hedland detention centre in Western Australia, after the discovery of their steel-hulled vessel last Thursday.
A number jumped overboard before immigration officials boarded the vessel.
Jeniene Butcher from Price of Wales Island says the man walked into her house yesterday morning.
Ms Butcher says she made him a sandwich, and talked in sign language until the police arrived. She says he knew only two English words "Sydney" and "work".
The remaining three boatpeople detained on Thursday Island are due to leave for Port Hedland today.
FEARS FOR SAFETY OF MISSING BABY

In Victoria, police hold grave fears for a missing baby boy, feared abducted from his Gippsland home early yesterday morning. 14-month old Jaidyn Leski was taken from his Newborough home, in Moe, after being left alone in the house while his mother's boyfriend went to pick up the mother.
When they returned at 3.30am the boy was gone, two front windows had been broken and a severed pig's head was found in the front garden.
Police will carry out a line search of the area this morning.
